subject: Accounting for Sample Overlap Between Summary Statistic Cohorts

messages.author: b0b4143f3aaa7ee5
messages.subject: Accounting for Sample Overlap Between Summary Statistic Cohorts
parts:
I'm running a user defined common factor model (bound residual variance) with three indicator variables. Two of the indicator variables have an overlap of samples. This is accounted in the ldsc function, with the following text from the GenomicSEM paper:

"The off-diagonal elements of VSLDSC are sampling covariances that indicate the extent
to which the sampling distributions of the variance and covariance estimates in
SLDSC co-vary with one another, as would be expected when there is overlap
among the samples from which the terms are estimated."

I'm curious about exactly how this is done. Can you share any documentation about this?

Furthermore, is there any options for LDSC, model fit, and/or GWAS functions that need to be kept in mind when having summary stats of cohorts with overlap samples?

I'm enjoying using GenomicSEM and it has added value to my research.


Thanks,
Ravi

messages.author: 0b5254eeb9973d7a
messages.subject: Re: Accounting for Sample Overlap Between Summary Statistic Cohorts
parts:
Hi Ravi,

The correction for sample overlap in models without SNPs is not an extra option but intrinsic in the estimation method. The correction for sample overlap in models with SNPs takes advantage of the cross-trait intercepts from LDSC to populate the relevant portions of Vfull. This is automated when using the functions that we provide for including SNPs in the model, and does not require special options.

You can read about how sample overlap factors into LDSC by looking into the original LDSC publications by Bulik Sullivan et al., and by reading more recent expositions such as https://doi.org/10.1101/310565.

The off-diagonal elements of Vldsc are estimated in multivariable LDSC through the same jacknife resampling as conventional LDSC. Resampling empirically estimates the sampling distribution of parameter estimates, so it is straightforward to estimate these distributions together for multiple parameters and obtain estimates of their dependencies (samping covariances). Our source code is open so you can examine the details of how this works if you are so inclined.

I believe that the formula for the sandwich correction of the GenomicSEM estimates using V is provided in the Grotzinger et al paper, and can also be found in our open source code. A great paper on how these corrections is the 2014 Savalei paper that we cite: https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2013.824793

Cheers,

Elliot

messages.author: b0b4143f3aaa7ee5
messages.subject: Re: Accounting for Sample Overlap Between Summary Statistic Cohorts
parts:
Elliot,

Thank you very much for the quick reply! These paper and links are very helpful!

I had another question related to this analysis. For one of my indicator variables, the summary statistics is a result of a sample size weighted meta-analysis using METAL. The phenotype is cases and controls. With this analysis for each SNP, I'm given the allele freq, sample size, effective sample size, z-score, p-value, direction of effect, and heterogeneity measures. I would like to use this cohort for a common factor GWAS model. I'm running into errors with the sumstats function, specifically since this input file does not have a standard error measurement. How would you recommend inputting this indicator? Would you recommend treating as a LPM model? Would you try to track down the standard errors? 

Any suggestions would be great appreciated.


Thank You,
Ravi
